title: Audiences in Paris and Guadeloupean beguine music
summary: Waters contrasts audiences now with then, recalls ten years at La Cigalle in Paris packed with Black soldiers, and describes beguine music played with a Guadeloupean trombonist.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. At that time the negroes appreciated more than they do now, you know what I mean? It's just, it's changed now, the white appreciate jazz more. You can tell by the audiences, I play ten countries a year for the last 15 years. And Paris, it's a lot of what not negroes, American negroes but there's a lot of black people. The West, Martinique is all black, mixed up like we are here, brown, black and all colors. The Guadaloupians the same thing, we have the Africans there. You have Cubans of all colors, they have all kinds of things, you know. But I played at the Cigalle in Paris for 10 years. And if it wasn't for the soldiers, Negro soldiers, that was based in Paris at that period, you wouldn't meet so many negroes anyplace, in the places we pack every night. It would hold about, at least 250, that's big for a cabaret, you hear?

See, they like the other music, they like their music. The Guadeloupe have their own thing, one of them, one of the music, one of the types of music that the Guadaloupians and the Martinique folks - they had a beguine, they call it, I think. A form of, I used to play it, I worked with one of those guys, you know, by the name of Albert Livrat [?]. We played beguines, it's a kind of a - well, I don't know, got a drum beat, it's somethin' like a bossa nova, you know. More, more than a bossa nova, more rhythm, you know. And that's them, that's their music. That's the music that they do, and they have, they have dances and they play that music, and the dances are crowded with Guadeloupe people and Martinique and African and so forth. But our place for the regular jazz, wasn't many - other than the American soldiers. It sometimes would be quite a few because American soldiers were based in [ ], before De Gaulle kicked them out, you know. It's now the base in Belgiums.
